paragraphs.text: יְשֻׂשׂ֥וּם מִדְבָּ֖ר וְצִיָּ֑ה וְתָגֵ֧ל עֲרָבָ֛ה וְתִפְרַ֖ח כַּחֲבַצָּֽלֶת׃

i18n.en: The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad, and the desert shall rejoice and blossom like the rose.
i18n.he: יְשֻׂשׂ֥וּם מִדְבָּ֖ר וְצִיָּ֑ה וְתָגֵ֧ל עֲרָבָ֛ה וְתִפְרַ֖ח כַּחֲבַצָּֽלֶת׃

notes.official:
*Yᵉśuśûm midbār wᵉṣiyyāh* “The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad”: the verb ends in *-m*. KJV reads it as an object suffix, “shall be glad for them,” while ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS render no suffix (all checked). The *-m* is usually explained as a dittography of the *m* of *midbār* or as an enclitic *mem*; the grammars were not checked here. The line renders no suffix and changes no consonant (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

The desert nouns follow the book. *Midbār* is “wilderness” and *ʿărāḇāh* “desert,” as at 35:6 and 40:3 (cf. 33:9 *kāʿărāḇāh*); at 43:19–20 the second noun of the pair is *yᵉšîmôn*, not *ʿărāḇāh*; *ʿărāḇāh* is a common noun here, not the place name “the Arabah.” *Ṣiyyāh* is “the dry land” with ASV; JPS 1917 has “the parched land,” and the stable 53:2 has “parched ground” for the phrase *ʾereṣ ṣiyyāh*. NJPS reorders the pair: “The arid desert shall be glad, The wilderness shall rejoice.” The verbs of joy are kept apart: *śûś* “be glad” (with *śāśôn* “gladness,” 35:10) and *gîl* “rejoice” (35:1–2).

*Kaḥăḇaṣṣeleṯ* “like the rose”: the flower is named only here and at Song 2:1, and its identification is uncertain. ASV, JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS print “rose,” and NJPS adds the note “Lit. ‘crocus’” (checked). The crocus, or another bulb plant such as the asphodel or narcissus, is the identification of modern lexica, and NRSV prints “crocus” (not verified). The line keeps the standard English and the botany stays here (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`).

paragraphs.translit: yəśuśūm midbār wəṣiyyāh wətāgēl ʿărābāh wətipraḥ kaḥăbaṣṣālet

paragraphs.text: פָּרֹ֨חַ תִּפְרַ֜ח וְתָגֵ֗ל אַ֚ף גִּילַ֣ת וְרַנֵּ֔ן כְּב֤וֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔הּ הֲדַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַשָּׁר֑וֹן הֵ֛מָּה יִרְא֥וּ כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הֲדַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing; the glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They shall see the glory of YHWH, the splendor of our God.
i18n.he: פָּרֹ֨חַ תִּפְרַ֜ח וְתָגֵ֗ל אַ֚ף גִּילַ֣ת וְרַנֵּ֔ן כְּב֤וֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔הּ הֲדַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַשָּׁר֑וֹן הֵ֛מָּה יִרְא֥וּ כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הֲדַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Pārōaḥ tip̄raḥ* “It shall blossom abundantly” puts the infinitive absolute before the finite verb of the same root (central `harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive`); ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render it “blossom abundantly.” In *ʾap̄ gîlaṯ wᵉrannēn* the form *gîlaṯ* looks like the construct of *gîlāh* “joy” and is often explained as an old absolute form (not verified). ASV and JPS 1917 render the phrase with nouns, “even with joy and singing,” and NJPS with verbs, “It shall also exult and shout” (checked). The line keeps ASV. The root *rnn* is “sing / singing” throughout the chapter (35:2, 6, 10).

The second half sets two nouns side by side twice. *Kᵉḇôḏ hallᵉḇānôn* is “the glory of Lebanon” (overlay `kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah`), and *hăḏar hakkarmel wᵉhaššārôn* is “the splendor of Carmel and Sharon.” Then *kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH hăḏar ʾĕlōhênû* is “the glory of YHWH, the splendor of our God” (central `kavod-yhwh`; overlay `hadar-splendor-isaiah`, `elohai-elohenu-doxology-isaiah-25`). The overlay entry for *hāḏār* cites this verse as its reason for keeping *kāḇôḏ* “glory” and *hāḏār* “splendor” apart. ASV and JPS 1917 have “excellency” for *hāḏār*, and NJPS has “splendor” at both sites (checked). The glory given to the land answers the glory of YHWH that the people will see.

*Hakkarmel* has the article, and in the stable chapters *hakkarmel* is the common noun “the fruitful field” (10:18; 29:17; 32:15–16). Here it stands between Lebanon and Sharon, both regions, and the line reads the place name Carmel with ASV, JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS (checked). The mountain takes the article elsewhere too (1 Kgs 18:19–20; Amos 1:2). Lebanon, Sharon and Carmel are the regions that wither at 33:9; here they give their glory to the desert. The play on “fruitful field” is left to the Hebrew. According to the online collation of 1QIsaᵃ (Fred P. Miller, *The Great Isaiah Scroll*, col. XXVIII, ao.net/~fmoeller; not checked against DJD 32), the scroll writes 35:1–2 in a compressed correction line and has *lᵉḇānôn* without the article (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim; claim type: speculative).** The canon does not cite Isa 35. *The Book Which Tells the Truth* reads “the glory of the God of Israel” coming “from the way of the east” in Ezek 43:2 as “the large ship respectfully called the «glory of God»” (TBWTT 3:193–194). It also quotes 1 Kgs 8:10–12, where the glory of YHWH and the cloud fill the temple, and reads the cloud as “a craft in orbit around the Earth” (TBWTT 3:104–107). The same verse also uses *kāḇôḏ* for “the glory of Lebanon,” the glory of a region given to the desert; the reader should weigh that use against the transfer. Reading “the glory of YHWH” that the people will “see” in Isa 35:2 in the same way extends those readings to a verse the canon does not discuss, so it is labelled speculative. The central `kavod-yhwh` entry records the standard sense, the visible presence of YHWH, and the line carries only the word “glory.”

notes.official: *Ḥazzᵉqû yāḏayim rāp̄ôṯ ûḇirkayim kōšᵉlôṯ ʾammēṣû* “Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees”: ASV has “confirm the feeble knees,” and JPS 1917 and NJPS have “make firm the tottering knees” (checked). The line takes the verb of JPS 1917, because “confirm” no longer means “make firm” in current English, and keeps ASV's “feeble” for *kōšᵉlôṯ*, literally “stumbling.” The plural imperatives do not name their addressees. paragraphs.text: אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי־לֵ֔ב חִזְק֖וּ אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ נָקָ֣ם יָב֔וֹא גְּמ֣וּל אֱלֹהִ֔ים ה֥וּא יָב֖וֹא וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Say to those who are of a fearful heart, “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God; he will come and save you.”
i18n.he: אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי־לֵ֔ב חִזְק֖וּ אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ נָקָ֣ם יָב֔וֹא גְּמ֣וּל אֱלֹהִ֔ים ה֥וּא יָב֖וֹא וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶֽם׃

notes.official:
*Nimhărê-lēḇ* “those who are of a fearful heart” (ASV, JPS 1917): the Niphal of *mhr* means “hasty,” and the phrase is literally “the hasty of heart,” people whom fear drives to panic. NJPS has “the anxious of heart” (checked). The same participle is “the rash” at 32:4 (*lᵉḇaḇ nimhārîm*), where the sense is thoughtless haste; here the parallel *ʾal-tîrāʾû* “do not fear” fixes the sense of fear. *Ḥizqû ʾal-tîrāʾû* is “Be strong, do not fear,” the modern form of ASV's “fear not,” as at 7:4, 40:9 and 43:1. The central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`, scoped to the formula “do not fear, for I am with you,” is not applied.

The syntax of *hinnēh ʾĕlōhêḵem nāqām yāḇôʾ gᵉmûl ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāḇôʾ wᵉyōšaʿăḵem* is disputed. ASV and JPS 1917 make “your God” the subject and *nāqām* an adverbial accusative: “your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God,” where ASV prints both “with”s as supplied words. NJPS reads an exclamation: “Behold your God! Requital is coming, The recompense of God— He Himself is coming to give you triumph” (checked). The Masoretic accents allow either: a disjunctive accent (*pashta*) stands on *ʾĕlōhêḵem*, and *nāqām* is joined to *yāḇôʾ*. The same exclamation, *hinnēh ʾĕlōhêḵem*, is “Behold your God!” at 40:9. The line keeps the construal of ASV and JPS 1917 and gives NJPS's here (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`). *Gᵉmûl* “recompense” is requital on the enemy and deliverance for the addressees. The suffixed *ʾĕlōhêḵem* is “your God” and the absolute *ʾĕlōhîm* is “God” (overlay `elohai-elohenu-doxology-isaiah-25`, `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). The whole message is set in quotation marks as embedded speech, as NJPS marks it; JPS 1917 quotes only ‘Be strong, fear not’ (checked) (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: ʾimrū lənimhărē-lēb ḥizqū ʾal-tīrāʾū hinnēh ʾĕlōhēkem nāqām yābōʾ gəmūl ʾĕlōhīm hūʾ yābōʾ wəyōšaʿăkem

paragraphs.text: אָ֥ז תִּפָּקַ֖חְנָה עֵינֵ֣י עִוְרִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י חֵרְשִׁ֖ים תִּפָּתַֽחְנָה׃

i18n.en: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
i18n.he: אָ֥ז תִּפָּקַ֖חְנָה עֵינֵ֣י עִוְרִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י חֵרְשִׁ֖ים תִּפָּתַֽחְנָה׃

notes.official: *ʾĀz tippāqaḥnāh ʿênê ʿiwrîm wᵉʾoznê ḥērᵉšîm tippāṯaḥnāh* “Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped” is the wording of ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (checked). The opening of blind eyes and deaf ears recurs in the book (29:18; 32:3; 42:7, 18) and reverses the commission of 6:10. Matt 11:5 and Luke 7:22 echo 35:5–6 (references recalled, not verified).

paragraphs.translit: ʾāz tippāqaḥnāh ʿēnē ʿiwrīm wəʾoznē ḥērəšīm tippātaḥnāh

paragraphs.text: אָ֣ז יְדַלֵּ֤ג כָּֽאַיָּל֙ פִּסֵּ֔חַ וְתָרֹ֖ן לְשׁ֣וֹן אִלֵּ֑ם כִּֽי־נִבְקְע֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ מַ֔יִם וּנְחָלִ֖ים בָּעֲרָבָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute shall sing; for in the wilderness waters shall break out, and streams in the desert.
i18n.he: אָ֣ז יְדַלֵּ֤ג כָּֽאַיָּל֙ פִּסֵּ֔חַ וְתָרֹ֖ן לְשׁ֣וֹן אִלֵּ֑ם כִּֽי־נִבְקְע֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ מַ֔יִם וּנְחָלִ֖ים בָּעֲרָבָֽה׃

notes.official: *ʾĀz yᵉḏallēḡ kāʾayyāl pissēaḥ* “Then the lame shall leap like a deer”: ASV and JPS 1917 have “the lame man … as a hart,” and NJPS has “the lame shall leap like a deer” (checked). *Pissēaḥ* is a generic singular, so the line drops the supplied “man” (wave I-4 ruling 13). *ʾAyyāl* “deer” and *ʾillēm* “the mute” (ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS “the dumb”) are the current English words. *Tārōn* “shall sing” is from *rnn*, as at 35:2 and 35:10; NJPS has “shall shout aloud.” *Kî-niḇqᵉʿû ḇammiḏbār mayim ûnᵉḥālîm bāʿărāḇāh* “for in the wilderness waters shall break out, and streams in the desert” repeats the wilderness–desert pair of 35:1. The online collation of 1QIsaᵃ (Fred P. Miller, *The Great Isaiah Scroll*, col. XXVIII, ao.net/~fmoeller; not checked against DJD 32) reports an extra verb, *yēlᵉḵû* “they shall go,” at the junction of 35:6 and 35:7, which the collator takes with the streams (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: ʾāz yədallēg kāʾayyāl pissēaḥ wətārōn ləšōn ʾillēm kī-nibqəʿū bammidbār mayim ūnəḥālīm bāʿărābāh

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרָב֙ לַאֲגַ֔ם וְצִמָּא֖וֹן לְמַבּ֣וּעֵי מָ֑יִם בִּנְוֵ֤ה תַנִּים֙ רִבְצָ֔הּ חָצִ֖יר לְקָנֶ֥ה וָגֹֽמֶא׃

i18n.en: And the glowing sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water; in the habitation of jackals, where they lay, grass shall become reeds and rushes.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרָב֙ לַאֲגַ֔ם וְצִמָּא֖וֹן לְמַבּ֣וּעֵי מָ֑יִם בִּנְוֵ֤ה תַנִּים֙ רִבְצָ֔הּ חָצִ֖יר לְקָנֶ֥ה וָגֹֽמֶא׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉhāyāh haššārāḇ laʾăḡam* “And the glowing sand shall become a pool”: *šārāḇ* occurs again only at 49:10, beside *šemeš* “sun.” ASV has “glowing sand,” JPS 1917 “parched land,” KJV “parched ground” and NJPS “Torrid earth” (checked). Arabic *sarāb* “mirage” lies behind the rendering “mirage” in some modern versions (not verified). The line keeps ASV. *Ṣimmāʾôn* is “the thirsty ground” (ASV, JPS 1917), and *mabbûʿê mayim* is “springs of water.”

The second half is a crux: *binwēh ṯannîm riḇṣāh ḥāṣîr lᵉqāneh wāḡōmeʾ*, word for word “in the abode of jackals, its resting place, grass / court to reed and papyrus.” *Tannîm* is the plural of *tan* “jackal” and is “jackals,” as at 13:22 and 43:20 and in the draft of 34:13. KJV's “dragons” (checked) confuses it with *tannîn* “sea monster, dragon” (27:1; Gen 1:21). The suffix of *riḇṣāh* is feminine singular and has no clear antecedent; ASV gives the sense, “where they lay,” and the collation reports *rēḇeṣ* without the suffix in 1QIsaᵃ (not checked against DJD 32).

*Ḥāṣîr* can be “grass” or “court, abode,” the word of 34:13 (*ḥāṣîr liḇnôṯ yaʿănāh* “a court for ostriches”). ASV reads “grass” and renders *lᵉ* as “with”: “shall be grass with reeds and rushes.” JPS 1917 and NJPS read “abode”: “It shall be an enclosure for reeds and rushes” and “The abode [of ostriches], reeds and rushes,” with the NJPS notes “Meaning of Heb. uncertain; emendation yields ‘a marsh’” and “Cf. 34.13” (checked). The line keeps ASV's “grass” and the Masoretic text but gives *lᵉ* the sense “become” that it has in the first two clauses of the verse (*laʾăḡam* “become a pool,” *lᵉmabbûʿê mayim* “springs of water”): “grass shall become reeds and rushes,” the wording of RSV, ESV and NRSVue (checked by the Reviewer). ASV's “with” is not the sense *lᵉ* has elsewhere in this verse. Either reading reverses 34:13, where Edom's ruins become the haunt of jackals and ostriches (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh haššārāb laʾăgam wəṣimmāʾōn ləmabbūʿē māyim binwēh tannīm ribṣāh ḥāṣīr ləqāneh wāgōmeʾ

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה־שָׁ֞ם מַסְל֣וּל וָדֶ֗רֶךְ וְדֶ֤רֶךְ הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ יִקָּ֣רֵא לָ֔הּ לֹֽא־יַעַבְרֶ֥נּוּ טָמֵ֖א וְהוּא־לָ֑מוֹ הֹלֵ֥ךְ דֶּ֛רֶךְ וֶאֱוִילִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִתְעֽוּ׃

i18n.en: And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called the Way of Holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it, but it shall be for them; the wayfarers, even fools, shall not go astray.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה־שָׁ֞ם מַסְל֣וּל וָדֶ֗רֶךְ וְדֶ֤רֶךְ הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ יִקָּ֣רֵא לָ֔הּ לֹֽא־יַעַבְרֶ֥נּוּ טָמֵ֖א וְהוּא־לָ֑מוֹ הֹלֵ֥ךְ דֶּ֛רֶךְ וֶאֱוִילִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִתְעֽוּ׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉhāyāh-šām maslûl wāḏereḵ* “And a highway shall be there, and a way” follows MT with ASV, JPS 1917 and KJV (checked). *Maslûl*, found only here, comes from *sll* “heap up (a road),” the root of *mᵉsillāh* “highway” (11:16; 19:23; 40:3); both take “highway.” Many commentators delete *wāḏereḵ* as a dittography of the following *wᵉḏereḵ* (not verified), and NJPS has only “a highway shall appear there” (checked). The online collation reports no variant at this word in 1QIsaᵃ, but a doubled *šāmmāh* “there” (Miller, col. XXVIII; not checked against DJD 32). The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Wᵉḏereḵ haqqōḏeš yiqqārēʾ lāh* “and it shall be called the Way of Holiness”: the verb of naming makes the phrase a name, so the line capitalises it, as it does “the City of Destruction” at 19:18 (overlay `ir-haheres-city-of-destruction-isaiah-19`). ASV and JPS 1917 print “The way of holiness,” NJPS “the Sacred Way” (checked) and NRSV “the Holy Way” (recalled). *Qōḏeš* is a noun and is “holiness,” as in *qōḏeš laYHWH* “holiness to YHWH” at 23:18.

The end of the verse is a crux. *Lōʾ-yaʿaḇrennû ṭāmēʾ wᵉhûʾ-lāmô hōlēḵ dereḵ waʾĕwîlîm lōʾ yiṯʿû* is literally “an unclean one shall not pass over it, and it (is) for them; one walking a way, and fools, shall not stray.” *Lāmô* “for them” has no stated antecedent. ASV supplies “for [the redeemed],” looking ahead to 35:9; KJV and JPS 1917 have “for those” and NJPS “for them,” with the notes “Emendation yields ‘for His people’” and “Meaning of Heb. uncertain” (checked). The line renders the Hebrew without ASV's supplied words: “but it shall be for them.” The main pause of the verse (*athnach*) falls on *lāmô*, so *hōlēḵ dereḵ* opens the last clause: “the wayfarers, even fools, shall not go astray.” This is the construal of ASV and JPS 1917 (“the wayfaring men, yea fools, shall not err therein”) without the gendered noun and the supplied “therein”; NJPS has “No traveler, not even fools, shall go astray.” The road through the desert takes up 40:3 and 43:19 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh-šām maslūl wāderek wəderek haqqōdeš yiqqārēʾ lāh lōʾ-yaʿabrennū ṭāmēʾ wəhūʾ-lāmō hōlēk derek weʾĕwīlīm lōʾ yitʿū

paragraphs.text: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה שָׁ֜ם אַרְיֵ֗ה וּפְרִ֤יץ חַיּוֹת֙ בַּֽל־יַעֲלֶ֔נָּה לֹ֥א תִמָּצֵ֖א שָׁ֑ם וְהָלְכ֖וּ גְּאוּלִֽים׃

i18n.en: No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up on it; they shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there.
i18n.he: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה שָׁ֜ם אַרְיֵ֗ה וּפְרִ֤יץ חַיּוֹת֙ בַּֽל־יַעֲלֶ֔נָּה לֹ֥א תִמָּצֵ֖א שָׁ֑ם וְהָלְכ֖וּ גְּאוּלִֽים׃

notes.official:
*Lōʾ-yihyeh šām ʾaryēh ûp̄ᵉrîṣ ḥayyôṯ bal-yaʿălennāh* “No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up on it”: *pᵉrîṣ ḥayyôṯ* is literally “the violent one of beasts.” ASV has “go up thereon” and NJPS “set foot on it” (checked). *Lōʾ timmāṣēʾ šām* is feminine singular, “it shall not be found there,” as KJV renders it (checked), with the beasts as a collective subject. ASV and JPS 1917 have “they shall not be found there” and NJPS “These shall not be found there”; the line keeps ASV's plural for the two animals named. *Wᵉhālᵉḵû gᵉʾûlîm* has no adverb. ASV prints “[there]” as a supplied word and NJPS has “walk it”; the line keeps ASV's adverb, which the English verb needs. The collation reports a double negative, *bal lōʾ*, in 1QIsaᵃ (Miller; not checked against DJD 32; overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Gᵉʾûlîm* “the redeemed” is the Qal passive participle of *gāʾal* (central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus`). The verb belongs to the kinsman who buys back what belonged to the family, and in Isaiah to YHWH, who buys back Israel (43:1; 44:22–23; 48:20). *Pᵉḏûyê YHWH* “the ransomed of YHWH” answers it at 35:10 (see there) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`).

paragraphs.translit: lōʾ-yihyeh šām ʾaryēh ūpərīṣ ḥayyōt bal-yaʿălennāh lōʾ timmāṣēʾ šām wəhāləkū gəʾūlīm

paragraphs.text: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשֻׁב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂ֔יגוּ וְנָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the ransomed of YHWH shall return, and come to Zion with singing, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
i18n.he: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשֻׁב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂ֔יגוּ וְנָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ (פ)

notes.official:
*Ûp̄ᵉḏûyê YHWH yᵉšuḇûn* “And the ransomed of YHWH shall return”: *pᵉḏûyê* is the Qal passive participle of *pāḏāh*, to set free by a payment or a substitute, the verb of the redemption of the firstborn (Exod 13:13–15; Num 18:15–17). ASV, JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS all have “the ransomed” here, and ASV has it at the duplicate 51:11 too (checked). They render the finite verb “redeem” (ASV 1:27; 29:22, checked). The central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus` gives *pāḏāh* “redeem” in the corpus, and the stable 1:27 and 29:22 print it. Applied here, that rule would give one English word to *gᵉʾûlîm* (35:9) and *pᵉḏûyê* (35:10) in adjacent verses, where the Hebrew pairs two roots. The line follows the versions with “the ransomed of YHWH,” and this wave proposes a context clause for the central entry: where *pāḏāh* and *gāʾal* stand in parallel, *pāḏāh* takes “ransom.” ASV draws the same line at Jer 31:11 (“hath ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him”), Hos 13:14 (“I will ransom them … I will redeem them”), Ps 69:19 (ASV 69:18) and Lev 27:27 (checked). The clause rests on ASV: KJV reverses the pair at 51:10–11 and Jer 31:11. The founder accepted the clause (sign-off 2026-11-26); it will govern 51:10–11.

The verse recurs almost word for word at 51:11, one of the links commentators draw between chs. 34–35 and chs. 40–55 (not verified). *Ûḇāʾû ṣiyyôn bᵉrinnāh* “and come to Zion with singing” uses *rnn* again (35:2, 6). *Wᵉśimḥaṯ ʿôlām ʿal-rōʾšām* is “and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads” (ASV, JPS 1917); NJPS has “Crowned with joy everlasting.” *Śāśôn wᵉśimḥāh* is “gladness and joy” with ASV and JPS 1917, and NJPS has “joy and gladness” (checked). In this chapter *śûś / śāśôn* is “be glad / gladness” (35:1, 10) and *śimḥāh* “joy.” The stable 22:13 renders the same pair the other way round, “joy and gladness”; no book entry fixes the joy vocabulary (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-35`). *Wᵉnāsû yāḡôn waʾănāḥāh* is “and sorrow and sighing shall flee away”; the collation reports a singular verb, *wᵉnās*, in 1QIsaᵃ (Miller; not checked against DJD 32; overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim; claim type: speculative).** The canon does not cite Isa 35. *The Book Which Tells the Truth* reads the ingathering oracle of Isa 43:5–7 as the return of the Jewish people and the creation of the State of Israel (TBWTT 5:25; cf. *Extraterrestrials Took Me to Their Planet* 2:124). Reading the return of “the ransomed of YHWH” to Zion in the same way extends that reading to a verse the canon does not cite, so it is labelled speculative. The line and the glossary carry only the Hebrew wording.

paragraphs.translit: ūpədūyē YHWH yəšubūn ūbāʾū ṣiyyōn bərinnāh wəśimḥat ʿōlām ʿal-rōʾšām śāśōn wəśimḥāh yaśśīgū wənāsū yāgōn waʾănāḥāh (p)
